decisions.statement: A path reading as no page file names no page.
A path with a section beside the page's own names no page.
A path the index files no page at names no page.
A page is read by its path rather than by the slug its name says.
The world is read rather than the disk.
An index that will not answer is refused with the reason rather than thrown.
A caller reading a page is handed the shape the index knows that page by.
The pages a key names are read from the property the key reaches.
The pages naming a path under one property are answered from the world's index.
A key reaching no property names no page.
Whether a key holds one value is read from the type the page states.
A key the page's type names under no property holds many values.
Nothing here works out a body.
Nothing here decides whether a page may be acted on.
Whether a page's type declares a key is read from that type.
A type the index cannot read judges no key.
A slug the page's type declares a key for answers that key.
A spelling that is already a key answers no key.
The value a key holds is read from the page type the property descends from.
The key a new key falls after is read from the pages of the page's own type.
A key falls after the last key more of those pages write before it than after it.
A key none of those pages write falls after nothing.
A key the page already writes falls after nothing.
No more than sixty-four of those pages are read.
Nothing here says where among a key's values a new value falls.

definition: the page a world's index answers at a path, and the pages on either side of that page's edges
